analysis:
The PR changes docs/reference/configuration.md only. The visible head text (lines 1-519) is documentation that predates the change. The changed range is head lines 553-555, which are outside the supplied units, so the new rows could not be examined directly. I reviewed the patch excerpt for them, but it is truncated.

The excerpt adds two variables, DARKBLOOM_TTFT_IDLE_CACHE_SWEEP and DARKBLOOM_TTFT_SEGMENT_RETENTION. Both are memory and performance controls, not auth, encryption or attestation controls. The excerpt says paged pools retain free KV segments, uncommitted and uncharged, up to min(2 GiB, slot grant/8). Retained segments are reinstalled at admission instead of newly allocated, filled and fenced. That touches T-028 (residual KV/GPU data) and TB-007.

The truncated text mentions zero-fill-on-demand host pages for new segments. It does not show whether retained segments are scrubbed or zeroed before reuse. Retention could widen cross-request KV residue within one provider process. This is an in-process, same-operator exposure, and the operator already sees plaintext in memory per T-014 and T-028. No concrete regression is established from docs alone.

The supplied documentation changes no sealed-prompt handling, SSD prefix-cache behavior (T-041), attestation or authorization. The prefix-cache text in the units is unchanged and still matches T-041: default-on, kill switch DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE=0, encrypted store. The new variables are said to be forwarded to the launchd job, but no PASSTHROUGH code is supplied.

Remaining question for integration: the code behind segment retention (EngineV2Factory+SegmentedBackend.swift) and the idle sweep (GlobalKVCacheBudget.swift, KVPoolReclaimer.swift) is not supplied. A reviewer should check whether retained, uncommitted KV segments are cleared or overwritten before reuse across requests, and whether this alters T-028. A reviewer should also check whether the retention interacts with the cacheSalt scope isolation. I raise no finding and mark this for deeper review because of that unverified contract.
